reviewer: Codex (primary-source and bilingual editorial review; not independent expert approval)

replication.mechanism: Running another model on prepared targets is a component of propagation; persistence against human intervention and failure of independent organizational controls require further evidence.
replication.conditions: Read the October 12 original, sections A–G and relevant Appendices A, C and F. GLM-5.2 acts from an external inference server, setting up Llama3.1-8B in an isolated eight-node Android-emulation environment with simplified access.
replication.counterexample: The harness starts the next agent after checks. A model that can set up inference may still be unable to run itself on a target, overcome real defenses or resist shutdown. The physical-device demonstration is separately arranged by researchers.
replication.evidence: Four of five GLM-5.2 trials reach the whole eight-node environment, one reaches seven. These are trial outcomes in the prepared environment, not counts of newly compromised organizations or ordinary deployment prevalence.
replication.limits: Experiment dates unspecified. Resistance to defenders is explicitly untested; a forecast from a general capability trend is not an observed replication deadline. No independent replication was verified in this bounded search.
replication.mitigation: Traffic observation, isolation and safer defaults are candidates in the original, not AI containment rates. The linked conventional-Mirai abstract cannot establish effectiveness against an adaptive AI; existing permission and resource controls remain candidates.
replication.readerContext: Both editions first explain continuing after a shutdown attempt and spreading beyond one organization. The new paragraphs identify researcher-provided access and startup rather than introducing an unexplained claim of autonomous escape.
replication.whyHere: C4a and C4b are the closest affected conditions, but this component capability does not establish either full condition. Add evidence and preserve hypothesis categories and the joint L-C4 relation.

primary.locator: Sections A–B; E–G; Appendices A, C and F
primary.support: Inference setup and simplified propagation, separate acting and served models, explicit absence of adversarial-defense testing.

safety.mechanism: An improved model can help propose and test safety interventions, provided its research transfers to safety problems and its results can be checked independently.
safety.conditions: Substantively reread the August 28 automated-alignment original and detailed methods, human comparison, cheating and limitations; reread the September pacing argument. R0-R4 reached its thirty-day date on October 13.
safety.counterexample: Better selected safety scores need not cover rare unknown failures, persist through further training or reduce actual incidents. Researcher cheating and a non-iterating human baseline constrain claims of autonomous superiority.
safety.evidence: The original reports improvements on defined failures with held-out tests and behavioral audits. Human-designed evaluations, capability checks, separate scoring and monitors remain in the loop. Pacing is a proposal rather than an effectiveness trial.
safety.limits: No guarantee that safety progress matches capability progress; no measurement of extinction-risk reduction. The detailed paper does not extensively test persistence after further reinforcement learning. No new independent replication verified.
safety.mitigation: Allocate resources to safety, retain separate evaluation and search for failures outside optimized scores. R4-C1 still requires actual implementation and persistent effects in use.
safety.readerContext: Read R4 and R0-R4 in Japanese and English. The text already explains why capability can support safety work without requiring the reader to infer that safety automatically accelerates.
safety.whyHere: Retain this conditional influence and its explanation after checking its positive evidence and limits. Advance only the due edge date, not unchanged source dates or all dependent item dates.

primary.support: Bounded safety-research improvements with external checks, cheating and generalization limits.

context.mechanism: Local failure, persistence despite shutdown and cross-organization spread combine before broad loss of control; separate conditions connect that to global harm.
context.conditions: Read the changed bilingual tour/detail context, L-C4, C4-H, R4-C1 and R0-R4, four affected graphs, three route definitions and the control story.
context.counterexample: Copied agents may remain containable; independent organizations may block spread. The same research capability can support defenses, and no replicated process necessarily reaches essential services.
context.evidence: The new capability experiment supports a narrower component than C4a or C4b. The due-edge evidence supports possible safety-research assistance rather than automatic matching progress. Existing summaries already preserve these distinctions.
context.limits: Separate experiments do not demonstrate simultaneous satisfaction of every AND condition. Metadata dependencies reaching the work graph do not constitute new labor-outcome evidence.
context.mitigation: Keep independent response capacity, resource revocation and outcome verification. Retain conditional global-harm bridges and safety-research mitigation requirements.
context.readerContext: Read the displayed sequence from local deviation to recovery and onward to harm in both editions. References to numbers and model names are explained in the research card, with plain-language boundaries in the node prose.
context.whyHere: Source and edge changes invalidate dependency fingerprints even when their conclusions remain appropriate. Retain topology, routes and categories after reading the affected contexts.

primary.support: Prepared propagation is not shutdown resistance or independent organizations losing control.
Limited safety assistance does not assure deployment prevention.

provenance.mechanism: Publication, experiment, source-check and item-review dates represent different claims. A new source does not refresh unrelated observations.
provenance.conditions: October 13 daily review, September 29–October 13 window. Reused draft PR #11 after fetching main and checking its ancestry, with the user checkout preserved. One edge was due.
provenance.counterexample: Index access cannot refresh scientific conclusions. A voluntary AISI agenda and a conventional-malware abstract cannot be promoted to new measured AI containment effectiveness.
provenance.evidence: Added one source/card and two bilingual node paragraphs; rereviewed and retained R0-R4. Preserved all thirty-four prior history translations and all evidence levels and topology.
provenance.limits: Eighteen daily starting pages and targeted searches are bounded coverage, not proof of no other correction. No full conventional-Mirai paper review, independent replication, browser layout test or public-production check claimed.
provenance.mitigation: Keep exact source and methods references, trial denominators, remaining uncertainties and before/after rationale. Validate content and build before updating the draft; never auto-merge.
provenance.readerContext: The history says what the experiment adds and what remains unproved. Technical details stay in the evidence card while the explanation identifies actors and the missing causal conditions.
provenance.whyHere: Metadata and history describe actual substantive work. The inventory retains hypothesis-level persistence and spread rather than treating a new date as observed loss of control.
